novel_features.name: Mining Stats Compound
novel_features.description: One command returns hashrate + difficulty + network hashrate + block height — formatted for n8n shell nodes, XEMD widgets, and agent consumption.
novel_features.rationale: No existing Dogecoin tool combines these into a single scriptable command with typed exit codes and --compact output.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when an n8n workflow needs a single snapshot of mining health without chaining multiple RPC calls.

novel_features.name: Peer Health Check
novel_features.description: Checks connected peer count and exits 0 (healthy) or 3 (below threshold) — n8n shell nodes branch on this exit code.
novel_features.rationale: Typed exit codes for n8n branching require machine-readable pass/fail signals; no existing tool does this.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use in n8n shell nodes to trigger peer-drop alerts without writing custom scripts.

novel_features.name: Blocks Found Window
novel_features.description: Detects if blocks were mined in a time window (--since 7d). Exit 0=found, exit 2=none found.
novel_features.rationale: Block window detection with typed exit codes is not available in any existing Dogecoin monitoring tool.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use in n8n to alert when no blocks have been found in the expected window — indicates mining pool issue.

novel_features.name: Hashrate History Trend
novel_features.description: Queries SQLite for historical hashrate over a time window — powers XEMD dashboard trend charts.
novel_features.rationale: Requires local SQLite time-series populated by sync; no existing Dogecoin tool stores and queries historical hashrate.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when an agent or dashboard needs hashrate trends, not just current snapshot.

novel_features.name: Difficulty Trend Alert
novel_features.description: Detects difficulty spikes or drops from SQLite history. Exit 0=stable, exit 5=significant change detected.
novel_features.rationale: Requires comparing multiple historical snapshots in local SQLite; no single RPC call provides this.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use to proactively alert when mining difficulty changes significantly, indicating network events.

novel_features.name: Mempool Status Compound
novel_features.description: Combines getmempoolinfo + estimatefee with human-readable fee tier labels (low/medium/high DOGE/KB).
novel_features.rationale: Combines two RPC calls into a single monitoring-friendly view with fee tier context.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use when planning coinbase transactions or monitoring network congestion.

novel_features.name: Node Doctor
novel_features.description: Version obsolescence check, auth validation, peer count, sync progress, and uptime in one command. Emits warning when node version is obsolete (< 1.14.0).
novel_features.rationale: Combines multiple RPC calls into a single diagnostic view with version threshold checking.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use for homelab monitoring; the version warning surfaces the upgrade requirement that the raw node surfaces only in errors fields.

narrative.headline: Monitor your Dogecoin node with typed exit codes, SQLite trending, and native MCP — everything bitcoin-cli lacks for automation.
narrative.value_prop: dogecoin-pp-cli wraps your Dogecoin Core JSON-RPC node in a monitoring-first CLI built for n8n workflows. Typed exit codes let shell nodes branch on peer health and block discovery. SQLite sync enables 30-day hashrate trends for dashboard widgets. Every command is agent-native via Homelab MCP.
narrative.auth_narrative: Set DOGECOIN_RPC_USER and DOGECOIN_RPC_PASS, or configure rpc_url/rpc_user/rpc_pass in ~/.config/dogecoin-pp-cli/config.toml. The node must accept HTTP Basic auth (configured via dogecoin.conf: rpcallowip, rpcuser, rpcpassword).

quickstart.comment: Check node health and version status first

troubleshoots.fix: Verify rpcallowip includes your client IP in dogecoin.conf
Check DOGECOIN_RPC_USER / DOGECOIN_RPC_PASS match dogecoin.conf rpcuser/rpcpassword
Node is running Dogecoin Core < 1.14.0; upgrade recommended but not required for monitoring
Node has fewer peers than --min-peers threshold; check Docker network / port exposure

narrative.when_to_use: Use dogecoin-pp-cli when n8n workflows need to branch on node state (peer health, block found, hashrate drop). Use when Homelab MCP sessions need to query mining state without writing custom scripts. Use when XEMD or Obsidian dashboards need historical trending that a single RPC call cannot provide.
